summary: Full text of the 2025 Clin Kidney J dose-response meta-analysis (10 randomized potassium-supplementation trials, 684 adults) shows a significant SBP reduction in hypertensive participants (-5.3 mmHg per +50 mmol/day urinary potassium, P=.02) and none in normotensive participants. Per Dr. Pham's revised 2026-10-28 ruling, urinary potassium as the exposure indicator limits dose equivalence but does not erase the BP finding, so the context is eligible for blood pressure in hypertensive adults only; Dose stays a separate judgment. A new applicability block records that population limit.

applicability.studied_population: Adults with hypertension in randomized potassium-supplementation trials (6 of 10 trials in PMID 40612568); BP benefit was not significant in normotensive adults, and exposure was measured as urinary potassium, so no supplement-dose equivalence is implied.

identity.preparation: Potassium interventions assessed through change in 24-hour urinary potassium excretion, not simply prescribed capsule mass.

population.description: 10 RCTs published 2000-2024, 684 adults (342 high-potassium, 342 control), mean age 26-66, mean BMI 22-31; 6 trials in people with hypertension and 4 without; UK, USA, Italy, China, Netherlands, Denmark. Pediatric populations excluded.

study_contexts.study_design: Systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis (linear, quadratic and cubic-spline models) of RCTs (9 crossover, 1 parallel; 1-6 weeks) that measured potassium intake change by 24-h urinary potassium excretion; sodium-plus-potassium interventions (salt substitutes, combined diets) excluded.

outcomes.name: Hypertensive subjects (6 trials): significant negative linear relation between urinary potassium increase and SBP (P=.02); per +50 mmol/day, SBP -5.31 mmHg (95% CI -9.85 to -0.77) and DBP -3.62 mmHg (-9.19 to 1.95, CI crosses zero).
Normotensive subjects (4 trials): slight non-significant linear relation (P=.48); per +50 mmol/day, SBP -0.54 (-2.03 to 0.96), DBP -0.12 (-1.47 to 1.22).

limitations: A 50 mmol urinary response is not an ingestion recommendation, minimum dose or label benchmark.
Preserve renal, medication and hyperkalemia safety assessment independently.

Historical bibliography census (not independent scoring sources; actual included-publication membership is separately bound to the inspected source table): 20673378, 33280043, 15740932, 25673113, 24048291, 20083724, 27867157, 22149452, 34064968, 27448942. Results Intervention Characteristics: high-potassium supplements were administered as potassium tablets or slow-released potassium tablets. This does not create a salt/mass or diet equivalence. Other included trials may not report a delivery form; this list does not establish one common preparation across all arms.

Dr. Pham revised ruling (fourth set, 2026-10-28): 40612568 pools randomized potassium-supplementation trials with urinary potassium as the exposure indicator; that limits dose equivalence but does not erase the BP findings. Evidence credit is for blood pressure in hypertensive adults only; Dose is a separate judgment; no cardiovascular-event credit; nutrition credit stays on its own pathway.

Small evidence base (10 short trials, 1-6 weeks), no pooled overall effect estimate; benefit seen only in hypertensive participants, with the DBP interval crossing zero. Not evidence for cardiovascular events.

Ingested supplement doses are not reported in the source; exposure is urinary potassium excretion difference. Berry 2010 included a fruit/vegetable arm and Stone 2021 a potato arm, so exposure is not exclusively supplemental.
Potassium supplements carry hyperkalemia risk in kidney disease and with ACE inhibitors, ARBs or potassium-sparing diuretics; this review did not assess safety, which stays with its own owner.
Context authored and source-verified by agent review (Claude) on 2026-10-28; Dr. Pham's pre-approval of fully source-verified contexts attested by Sean on 2026-10-28.

dose.administration_frequency: Trial-specific daily oral potassium supplementation for 1-6 weeks; no single pooled schedule (Table 1; Results 'Description of potassium intake modification').
co_therapies: Participants generally kept usual diet and activity; some trials had run-in and washout periods. Vongpatanasin 2016 used potassium magnesium citrate (magnesium co-exposure). Medication eligibility varied by trial.
dose.reported_regimen: Potassium chloride, aspartate or bicarbonate supplements given as tablets or slow-release tablets (one trial also used potassium-rich fruit/vegetables or potato). Exposure is the between-arm difference in 24-h urinary potassium excretion: 12.5-92 mmol/day overall (30-92 without hypertension, 12.5-45 with hypertension). Ingested supplement amounts are not tabulated in the source.

normalization.basis: Source exposure metric is measured urinary potassium excretion difference, not ingested mass; no conversion to a label dose, minimum or benchmark is made.
